title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 77-79). This is §6 of the 'Teichmülleries' notes. P = (S, A, R ⊂ S×A) is a finite combinatorial n-gon (n ≥ 3), with vertex set S, edge set A and incidence relation R. D is its dihedral automorphism group of order 2n, and D^+ is the cyclic rotation subgroup. The two orientations of P are identified with the two privileged generators ω, ω' of D^+, the rotations by one step.

The previous page asserts that there is a complex projective line Σ = Σ_P, unique up to unique isomorphism, with S ↪ Σ, such that the D-action extends to complex automorphisms. Concretely Σ ≅ P^1_C, S is μ_n, and D is the holomorphic dihedral group generated by z ↦ ζz and z ↦ 1/z.

This page continues as follows.
(i) The vertices and the arcs of great circle joining them lie on one circle. That circle gives a cellular subdivision of itself and defines a canonical real structure on Σ, whose real locus is denoted Σ(R) or Σ_R (≅ P^1(R) ⊃ μ_n after a Möbius change; the unit circle in the model).
(ii) There is a unique homogeneous (round) Riemannian metric on Σ invariant under D, and Σ_R is a great circle for it.
(iii) Σ_R cuts Σ into two open hemispheres. These correspond bijectively to the two orientations by the 'Stokes correspondence' (49): π_0(Σ∖Σ_R) ≅ ω. A hemisphere corresponds to the orientation of its boundary circle given by Stokes' convention, which in turn is an orientation of the polygon.
(iv) The fixed-point set of the rotations has exactly two points, one in each open hemisphere (the poles 0 and ∞). Hence (50): Σ^{D} ≅ ω, and P_ω denotes the pole attached to ω. It is characterized intrinsically: the action of ω on the tangent space T_{P_ω}Σ is rotation by +2π/n, whereas at P_{ω'} it is rotation by −2π/n.
(v) Notation: R_s ∈ Σ_R is the point of vertex s, and Q_a is the midpoint of edge a.

Purpose: the next page studies the fundamental groupoids of Σ* = Σ∖S (≅ P^1 minus μ_n). It uses the base points P_ω and the 'mixed' (equivariant/orbifold) fundamental groups under {1,τ}, D, and D×{1,τ} (order 4n), where τ is complex conjugation for the canonical real structure. The goal is a canonical, choice-free description of the cyclotomic genus-0 building blocks ('carte cyclotomique') for the Teichmüller tower / Galois-action programme.
errors: If D acts on Σ by complex (holomorphic) automorphisms, as stated on p.77 and confirmed on p.79 (D_P is the orientation-preserving subgroup of D×{1,τ}), then the orientation-reversing elements of D act as half-turns about equatorial axes. These exchange the two poles, so Σ^D = ∅, not a 2-point set.
The chain Σ^D = Σ^{D^+} as written is therefore wrong; the correct statement is Σ^{D^+} = Σ^{ω} = Σ^{{ω}} (card 2).
Formula (50) should then be read as a D-equivariant bijection Σ^{D^+} ≅ ω. Reflections swap both the orientations and the poles, which is consistent with the Stokes correspondence (49).
A literal bijection between the fixed set of D and ω could not be D-equivariant, since D acts non-trivially on ω. So the superscript D in Σ^D must be a slip for D^+.
Otherwise the claims (unique round metric, Σ_R a great circle, tangent rotation ±2π/n at the poles) are correct.

ideas.what: Canonical realization of a combinatorial n-gon on P^1_C with dihedral symmetry: vertices as μ_n on a great circle, inducing a canonical real structure and round metric
ideas.modern_name: regular dihedral (Platonic) action on the Riemann sphere; P^1 minus μ_n with its real structure
ideas.where_published: related ideas on regular maps/polygons and genus-0 cyclotomic pieces appear in Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

ideas.what: Stokes correspondence: the hemispheres (components of Σ∖Σ_R) correspond to the orientations of the polygon via the induced boundary orientation
ideas.modern_name: boundary orientation convention / complex orientation of the components of Σ∖Σ(R)

ideas.what: Base points P_ω at the fixed points of the rotation group, characterized by the tangent rotation angle +2π/n; preparation for mixed (equivariant) fundamental groups π_1(Σ*, D×{1,τ}; P_ω)
ideas.modern_name: orbifold/equivariant fundamental group of [ (P^1∖μ_n) / (D_n × Z/2) ] with base point at 0/∞

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up, in a choice-free way, the full symmetry group D_n×{1,τ} (order 4n) of P^1 minus μ_n, with base points at the fixed points 0, ∞ labelled by orientations. He intends to study the corresponding mixed fundamental groups. This anticipates the dihedral symmetry of π_1(P^1∖{0,∞,μ_N}) exploited later by Goncharov (dihedral Lie algebras) and by work on motivic multiple zeta values at roots of unity. The page itself contains only the setup.
missed.quote: on désignera par P_ω le point de Σ^D qui correspond à ω ∈ ω. Il est caractérisé par le fait que l'opération de ω dans l'espace tangent à Σ en P_ω est une rotation d'angle +2π/n
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early, intrinsic (orientation-labelled) formulation of the dihedral and real symmetry of the cyclotomic fundamental group. Its relevance depends on what the following pages derive; the page itself has no new result.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but elementary setup: dihedral group on the Riemann sphere, real structure, poles labelled by orientations. It contains a minor slip (Σ^D should be Σ^{D^+}). Its interest lies only in being the preparation for equivariant π_1 of the cyclotomic sphere in the Teichmüller programme.
transcription_corrections: 'la génératrice de ω dans l'espace tangent' should read 'l'opération de ω dans l'espace tangent à Σ en P_ω est une rotation d'angle +2π/n'.

The inserted marginal phrase after 'Σ,' is hard to read and is not reliably 'il est donc (à fortiori, canoniquement isomorphe)'. It seems to read 'il est donc ... (c'est-à-dire ... canoniquement près?)' and should be marked uncertain.
Line 4: the insertion above the deleted word is 'ou Σ_R', i.e. 'noté Σ(R) ou Σ_R'.
